column2: How do I open my family tree on another computer in my home?
column3: On the computer that keeps the family tree: Settings → 🖧 Several computers, then turn on the switch (it is off at first, and the family tree must have a password). The app shows an address (for example http://192.168.1.20:47321) and an invitation code. On the other computer, type this address in a browser, then the code and a name: a 6-digit code appears on both sides. If it is the same, click “✓ Allow” on the main computer; the other computer then gives the family tree’s password. Only over your home Wi-Fi, never over the internet; everything cuts off when the main computer goes to sleep or closes the app. In this version, the other devices are read-only, and what travels over the Wi-Fi is not encrypted: never open it on a public Wi-Fi.

column2: How do I allow or remove a device, and what can it do?
column3: Settings → 🖧 Several computers → Allowed devices: each accepted device, its address, its last visit. “Remove” cuts it off at once (“↶ Undo” for 10 seconds). A guest device sees everything, read-only: it changes nothing, exports nothing, changes neither family tree nor settings, and touches neither the password nor the backups. Each device gives the family tree’s password itself. 📜 Who saw what records the connections with the device’s name. A request without an answer disappears after 2 minutes; after 5 refusals or 5 wrong codes, no more requests for 15 minutes.
